research_rationale:
Executive Order 12657 of November 18, 1988 (53 FR 47513, Federal Register Vol. 53 No. 226, Wednesday November 23, 1988) directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (since 2003 the Department of Homeland Security) to assist emergency preparedness planning at commercial nuclear power plants when State or local governments decline or fail to prepare adequate plans. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (pages 47513-47516) with title, preamble, sections 1 to 9 and the White House dateline present, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed as a note to 42 U.S.C. 5195, stated as amended by Executive Order 13286 section 41; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held. The held current CFR sections 44 CFR 352.3 and 352.28 cite the order, and the current predicate cited for other clauses is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). The only later amendment found in the held official texts is Executive Order 13286 section 41 (effective March 1, 2003), which replaced FEMA and its Director with the Department of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Homeland Security throughout sections 1(b) to 6; it is recorded as a later event on every clause containing those words. The packet chain also lists Executive Order 12977 as an amender, but the text of Executive Order 12977 (1995) does not amend this order; the item comes from a held source-ladder text of Executive Order 13286 mislabeled with that number, and the claim does not rely on it. No held source revokes or supersedes the order. Section 6(a) to (c) are implementation commands whose performance dates are not shown in held sources; they are carried as continuing on a disclosed limited basis, not as ended.
